concepts.title: Quantisation of Electric Charge
concepts.definition: Every free charge comes in whole-number multiples of a fixed elementary value e, so the net charge of a body can change only in steps of that quantum.
concepts.key_idea: Charge is grainy at the microscopic scale, yet the step size 1.6e-19 C is so tiny that macroscopic charges look continuous.
question_patterns: how many electrons must be removed to leave a charge of 2 microcoulomb on a body
calculate the number of electrons transferred when a rubbed polythene piece picks up 3 times 10 to the minus 7 coulomb
a body carries a net charge of 1.6 nanocoulomb; find the count of excess electrons on it
determine how many elementary charges make up a total charge of 8 times 10 to the minus 12 coulomb
estimate the electron count matching a total charge of minus 1 coulomb
use the charge quantum to turn a body net charge into a count of excess electrons sitting on it

solution_steps.explain: each electron carries e = 1.6e-19 C

solution_steps.action: divide the net charge by the quantum
solution_steps.explain: the integer count of electrons is the net charge split into quanta of e

concepts.title: Additivity and Conservation of Charge
concepts.definition: Charges combine like plain signed numbers, and the algebraic total held by an isolated setup stays fixed no matter how the charges rearrange inside it.
concepts.key_idea: Rubbing or internal reactions only relocate charge between bodies; the overall bookkeeping of an isolated system never changes.
question_patterns: find the algebraic total of several signed charges in one isolated system and say why that total cannot change
why does the total charge of an isolated system stay constant during rubbing
explain charge conservation when a neutron decays into a proton plus an electron
a system holds five charges with mixed signs; how do you obtain the net charge
does charging a body by friction create fresh charge or only shift it between objects

solution_steps.action: attach the algebraic sign to every charge
solution_steps.explain: positive and negative signs decide each contribution, so addition is scalar with signs
the total is the plain arithmetic sum, since charge has magnitude but no direction

solution_steps.action: compare totals before and after the process
solution_steps.explain: an isolated system shows the same total before and after, which is the conservation check

concepts.title: Coulomb Force Between Point Charges
concepts.definition: The push or pull between two point charges grows with the product of the charges, falls off as the square of the gap, and acts along the line joining them.
concepts.key_idea: With k about 9e9 in SI units, two 1 C charges one metre apart repel with roughly 9e9 N, which is why the coulomb is a very large unit.
question_patterns: find the mutual force between two small charged spheres 30 cm apart carrying 2 times 10 to the minus 7 and 3 times 10 to the minus 7 coulomb
calculate the electrostatic force between two point charges separated by a given distance in air
what is the repulsion between two like charges of 1 microcoulomb kept 10 cm apart
compute the Coulomb force between charges q1 and q2 placed r metres apart in vacuum
determine how strongly two point charges attract when their values and separation are known
evaluate the inverse-square electric force for a pair of tiny charged bodies

solution_steps.explain: k = 1/(4 pi eps0) is about 9e9 N m^2 per C^2 in SI units
the inverse-square law uses the gap between centres raised to power two

solution_steps.action: combine charges over the squared gap
solution_steps.explain: multiply the constant by both charges and divide by the squared separation to get the force magnitude

concepts.title: Superposition Principle for Many Charges
concepts.definition: With several charges present, you get the force on any one of them by adding, as vectors, every pairwise Coulomb force, each pair behaving as though the others were absent.
concepts.key_idea: Pairwise forces stay unaffected by onlooker charges, so a many-charge problem reduces to vector addition of two-body results.
question_patterns: find the resultant force on a charge placed at the centre of a square with charges at its corners
how do you add the forces on one charge from several neighbouring charges
name the principle used to obtain the net force in a many-charge system
three equal charges sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle; describe the net force on a charge at the centroid
why is the force between a given pair of charges unchanged when a third charge is brought nearby

solution_steps.action: draw the pairwise force on the target charge
solution_steps.explain: for every other charge, write the two-body Coulomb force vector with its direction

solution_steps.action: add the vectors by the parallelogram rule
solution_steps.explain: each pairwise force ignores the remaining charges, so straight vector addition is valid

solution_steps.action: read the net force from the vector sum
solution_steps.explain: symmetric arrangements can make the vector sum exactly zero

concepts.title: Electric Field of a Point Charge
concepts.definition: A source charge fills the region around itself with a field, meaning the force per unit positive charge that a tiny test charge would feel at each point, directed radially for a point source.
concepts.key_idea: Field strength follows the same inverse-square falloff as the force, pointing outward for a positive source and inward for a negative one.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.7 (electric field, E = kQ/r^2, F = qE)
question_patterns: calculate the electric field intensity at 30 cm from a point charge of 2 nanocoulomb
what field does a point source charge produce at a stated distance in free space
find E at a point 20 cm away from a 5 microcoulomb charge
determine the field strength at radius r around a point charge Q
compute the magnitude of the electric field due to a 1.6 times 10 to the minus 19 coulomb charge at 1 angstrom

solution_steps.explain: the field of a point source is the force law with one charge removed, so k enters directly
multiply k by the source charge and split by r squared to get the field at that radius

concepts.title: Charged Particle Falling in a Uniform Field
concepts.definition: Inside a uniform field a particle of charge q feels the steady force qE, so it speeds up uniformly with acceleration qE/m just like a body under constant gravity.
concepts.key_idea: A heavier particle needs more time to cross the same gap from rest, the opposite of free fall where mass cancels out.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt Example 1.7 (electron and proton fall times in uniform field)
question_patterns: an electron falls through 1.5 cm in a uniform field of 2 times 10 to the 4 newton per coulomb; find its time of fall
how long does a proton take to cover the same distance in a reversed uniform field
find the acceleration of a charged particle released in a uniform electric field
compute the time a charge needs to travel distance h from rest inside a constant field
compare the fall times of an electron and a proton crossing the same gap in a uniform field

solution_steps.explain: force is qE, so dividing by the mass gives the constant acceleration of the particle
starting from rest, distance h = 0.5 a t^2, so the time is the square root of 2h over a

concepts.title: Electric Field Lines and Their Rules
concepts.definition: A field line is a curve whose tangent at every point shows the net field direction there; crowding of lines marks where the field is stronger.
concepts.key_idea: Lines run from positive to negative charge, never cross one another, and never close into loops in electrostatics.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.8 (electric field lines, properties list)
question_patterns: why can two electric field lines never intersect each other
do electrostatic field lines form closed loops, and why not
what does the crowding of field lines at a point indicate about the field
where do field lines begin and end for an isolated single charge
describe the field line picture around a pair of equal and opposite charges

solution_steps.explain: the direction of E at any point is the tangent to the line there, so one point cannot hold two directions
crossing lines would give two field directions at the crossing point, which is impossible
lines start on positive and finish on negative charge and stay open curves in electrostatics

concepts.title: Electric Flux Through a Flat Surface
concepts.definition: Electric flux measures how much field pierces a given area, scaling with the field strength, the area, and the cosine of the tilt between them.
concepts.key_idea: Turn a surface edge-on to the field, ninety degrees tilt, and the flux through it drops to zero.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.9 (electric flux, delta phi = E . dS)
question_patterns: find the flux of a uniform field through a square of side 10 cm held parallel to the yz plane
calculate the electric flux through a flat area tilted at 60 degrees to a uniform field
what flux passes through an area of 0.01 metre squared inside a field of 3 times 10 to the 3 newton per coulomb
compute the flux through a tilted surface placed in a steady uniform field
a square frame is held edge-on to a uniform field; how much flux goes through it

solution_steps.action: project the area normal to the field
solution_steps.explain: only the component of area facing the field passes lines, so multiply the area by the cosine of the tilt
the flux equals the field strength times the area projected perpendicular to it

concepts.title: Electric Dipole Moment
concepts.definition: For two charges matching in size but opposite in sign, held a fixed distance apart, the dipole moment equals charge times separation and points from the negative member toward the positive one.
concepts.key_idea: The moment, not the separate charges, decides the far field of the pair; a dipole can carry zero net charge yet nonzero moment.
question_patterns: find the dipole moment of two charges plus and minus 2.5 times 10 to the minus 7 coulomb kept 30 cm apart
calculate p for a pair of equal and opposite charges with a stated separation
what is the moment of a dipole whose charges are 1 microcoulomb and separation 5 mm
two charges of plus 10 and minus 10 microcoulomb sit 5 mm apart; obtain the dipole moment
state the direction of the dipole moment vector for a given charge pair

solution_steps.explain: the magnitude of the moment is the charge times the gap 2a between the pair members

concepts.title: Dipole Field at a Far Axial Point
concepts.definition: Far from a dipole, on the line through both charges, the field weakens as the cube of the distance, runs parallel to the moment, and is twice the equatorial value there.
concepts.key_idea: Dipole fields die off like 1/r cubed, one power faster than the 1/r squared falloff of a single charge.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.10.1 (field on the axis, Eq. 1.15 and 1.20)
question_patterns: calculate the field on the axis of a dipole 15 cm from its centre for charges of 10 microcoulomb held 5 mm apart
find the electric field at a far axial point of a short dipole
what is the axial field at distance r from the centre of a dipole of moment p
compute the field along the dipole axis when r is much larger than the half separation
how strong is the field at a far point lying on the line through both charges of a short dipole

solution_steps.explain: the moment is charge times full separation, needed because the far field depends on the product qa
twice k times the moment divided by the cube of the axial distance gives the field on the axis

concepts.title: Torque on a Dipole in a Uniform Field
concepts.definition: A uniform field cannot translate a dipole but does twist it; the turning effect peaks when the moment sits crosswise to the field and vanishes once they line up.
concepts.key_idea: The torque is the cross of moment with field, so aligned orientation is the zero-torque, favoured state.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.11 (dipole in uniform external field, Eq. 1.22)
question_patterns: calculate the torque on a dipole of moment 4 times 10 to the minus 9 coulomb metre aligned at 30 degrees inside a field of 5 times 10 to the 4 newton per coulomb
find the turning effect on a dipole held at an angle to a uniform field
at what orientation of the dipole moment is the torque maximum
compute the couple acting on an electric dipole placed in a steady field
when is the torque on a dipole inside a uniform field equal to zero

solution_steps.action: combine moment, field and the sine of the angle
solution_steps.explain: each charge feels qE in opposite directions, giving a couple of size pE sin(theta)

concepts.title: Gauss Law: Enclosed Charge from Flux
concepts.definition: The net flux leaving any closed surface is fixed by the total charge trapped inside it, regardless of the surface shape or where the charges sit within.
concepts.key_idea: Dividing the net outward flux by eps0 recovers the enclosed charge; zero net flux means zero net enclosed charge.
question_patterns: the net outward flux through a closed box is 8 times 10 to the 3 newton metre squared per coulomb; find the charge inside
use Gauss law to obtain the net charge enclosed from a measured total flux
a point charge gives a flux of minus 1 times 10 to the 3 through a sphere centred on it; what is the charge value
how much charge sits inside a Gaussian cube when the total flux through it is known
measured outward flux through a closed bag-shaped surface; work out the charge caught inside

solution_steps.explain: Gauss law says flux equals enclosed charge over eps0, so multiply the net flux by 8.854e-12

concepts.title: Field of an Infinite Charged Wire
concepts.definition: An endlessly long, evenly charged straight wire pushes test charges radially outward with a strength that falls off only as the first power of the perpendicular distance.
concepts.key_idea: Cylindrical symmetry makes the falloff 1/r instead of 1/r squared; k still stands for 1 over 4 pi eps0.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.14.1 (field of an infinitely long straight wire, Eq. 1.32)
question_patterns: for a very long evenly charged straight wire, compute the radial field 5 cm out when each metre carries 2 microcoulomb
get the electric field at distance r from an endless line of charge carrying lambda coulomb per metre
use cylindrical symmetry to state how the field of a charged wire varies with distance and evaluate it at 2 cm for density 2 microcoulomb per metre
work out the strength of the radial field around an infinite line of charge at a given perpendicular distance
how much field does a wire with endless length and steady charge density create 10 cm from itself
evaluate the one-over-r falloff field near a straight charged wire of great length at radius r

solution_steps.explain: the wire result is usually quoted as lambda over 2 pi eps0 r, which equals 2k lambda over r

solution_steps.action: double k times density over distance
solution_steps.explain: multiply 2k by the charge per unit length and divide by the perpendicular distance

concepts.title: Field of a Charged Plane Sheet
concepts.definition: An endless flat sheet with even surface charge gives a field on each side that is constant, no matter how far from the sheet the point lies.
concepts.key_idea: Twice eps0 in the denominator, and the result is independent of distance, pointing away from the sheet on both faces for positive sigma.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.14.2 (field of a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet, Eq. 1.33)
question_patterns: find the field near a large flat sheet with surface charge density 17 times 10 to the minus 22 coulomb per metre squared
calculate E produced by an infinite plane sheet of charge with a stated sigma
what is the field on either side of a uniformly charged infinite sheet
compute the steady field close to a big evenly charged plate
state the value of the field due to an endless uniformly charged flat sheet at any distance

solution_steps.action: divide the surface density by twice eps0
solution_steps.explain: Gauss law across a pillbox straddling the sheet gives sigma over 2 eps0, with 2 eps0 = 1.7708e-11

concepts.title: Field of a Charged Spherical Shell
concepts.definition: Outside a thin spherical shell carrying charge spread evenly over it, the field matches that of a point charge seated at the centre, while every interior point feels exactly zero field.
concepts.key_idea: Spherical symmetry plus Gauss law forces a zero interior field, the electrical twin of the gravitational shell theorem.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph101.txt section 1.14.3 (field of a uniformly charged thin spherical shell, Eq. 1.34-1.35)
question_patterns: calculate the electric field outside a thin spherical shell of radius R carrying total charge q
what field does a charged spherical shell produce at an external point
compute E at distance r greater than R from a shell with surface density sigma
find the outside field of a uniformly charged sphere 2.4 m across with 80 microcoulomb per metre squared on its surface
determine the field 20 cm from the centre of a charged sphere of radius 10 cm and known surface density

solution_steps.action: total the charge on the shell
solution_steps.explain: surface density times the shell area 4 pi R squared gives the whole charge, using 4 pi = 12.566371

solution_steps.action: treat the shell as a central point charge
solution_steps.explain: for exterior points the whole charge behaves as if seated at the centre, so use the point-charge field
